# How stable is the top 20? (generated by src/stability.py)

Census numbers are estimates with margins of error. We redrew every tract's no-vehicle share within its margin 1000 times and recomputed the ranking with the same formula.

- On average 16.3 of the 20 published top stops stay in the top 20 (range 4 to 20).
- 12 of the 20 stay in the top 20 in at least 80 percent of draws.
- 2 of 58 tracts have a margin of error of 15 points or more on their no-vehicle share; they are small tracts, often campus tracts with few households.
- The tract with the most top-20 stops has 164 households and a margin of error of 16.9 points.

Only census uncertainty is varied. Temperature, bus visits and shelter status are held fixed, so this tests one input, not the whole ranking. The published ranking is unchanged.

Per-stop numbers are in `outputs/ranking_stability.csv`.
